packs.title: Rock, Hill and Shore
packs.promise: Read Edinburgh from its castle rock and old volcano to a river path and the sea.

q.s: Find three castle features from three different centuries and put them in time order.
st: Enter with your ticket and follow the route up to the top of the rock.
Find St Margaret’s Chapel and the great siege gun Mons Meg outside it, and note the date each display gives.
Find the One O’Clock Gun on Mills Mount Battery and note when its time signal began.
Put the three features in time order and add one line on what each was made for.

q.t: The Outline of an Old Volcano
q.s: Draw the skyline of Arthur’s Seat and the crags from the loch path, then mark the chapel ruin.
st: Walk to the loch-side path with a clear view up to Arthur’s Seat.
Trace the hill’s outline with one continuous line from left to right.
Add the crags and mark the small ruined chapel on the slope above the loch.
Label the highest point and write the date.

q.s: Find three garden places and name one city landmark you can pick out from the high viewpoint.
st: Enter by the East Gate on Inverleith Row or the West Gate on Arboretum Place.
At the Chinese Hillside, record one plant or water detail from its planting or the water at its foot.
At the Rock Garden, record one stone or alpine-plant detail.
Climb to the high viewpoint, find the city skyline and name one landmark you can pick out.

packs.title: Leith and Newhaven
packs.promise: Spend two afternoons in Edinburgh’s port: its links, quays, docks and fishing harbour.

q.s: Find both grassy mounds, read their plinths, then check the official record for the doubt.
st: Walk to the south side of Leith Links.
Find the steeper, flat-topped western mound and read its interpretation plinth.
Walk about 250 m east to the gentler mound and read its plinth.
Record what the plinths say the mounds were. Then compare them with the Historic Environment Scotland record linked in this quest, and note one reason it gives for questioning that story.

q.s: Ride from Foot of the Walk to Newhaven and note how the view changes from street to docks and harbour.
st: Buy a ticket, or tap on with your contactless card or device at the Foot of the Walk platform validator, then board towards Newhaven.
From wherever you can see out, list the stops in order.

Note where the street gives way to docks or harbour buildings, and the stop where you first see open water. If buildings, hoardings or a crowded tram hide the water, write ‘no water seen’ instead; that earns the same credit.
Get off at Newhaven and, if you paid contactless, tap off at the platform validator with the same card or device before walking to the harbour.

q.s: Draw Newhaven’s two harbour lights side by side and label how they differ.
st: Walk to the harbour and find a spot where you can see both lights.
Draw the short round stone light and the taller tiered iron lighthouse side by side.
Label two differences in shape and one in material.
Add the boats or water you can see between them.
